_description: Capital gains (brokerage withdrawals) must enter SS provisional income. Single filer drawing SS alongside a taxable account — the brokerage pull is part of AGI and so makes a portion of SS taxable, even though it is itself taxed at LTCG rates.
_rationale: Single, Florida, age 65. SS $40k/yr (haircut disabled), spending $63.5k/yr, only account is brokerage (treated as 100% gain). SS gross $40k covers part of spending; the $23.5k gap is pulled from brokerage. IRS provisional income = AGI-ex-SS + 0.5*SS = $23.5k LTCG + $20k = $43.5k, above the single 85% threshold ($34k). SS taxable = min(0.85*($43.5k - $34k) + min($4.5k base, 0.5*$40k), 0.85*$40k) = min($8,075 + $4,500, $34,000) = $12,575. longTermCapGainsRate = 0 isolates the provisional mechanic (no LTCG tax), and the $12,575 taxable SS sits below the single 65+ standard deduction, so federal tax = $0 and there is no withdrawal feedback — the brokerage pull is exactly $23,500. End-of-year balance = $500,000 - $23,500 = $476,500. BEFORE the fix, brokerage was excluded from provisional income: provisional = 0.5*$40k = $20k < $25k threshold → zone 'none' → $0 SS taxable (the tax torpedo was invisible for brokerage-funded spending). 0% growth, 0% inflation, IRMAA/NIIT off.
name: SS Provisional Includes LTCG
